description: Show what you are drawing in Discord as Rich Presence
name: Discord presence
panel.appIdRequired: Rich Presence needs your own Discord application. Create one in the Developer Portal and paste its Application ID here.
panel.assetHint: Upload the images under Rich Presence → Art Assets in the Developer Portal, then use their names here. An empty field hides the image.
panel.showLinkNote: Rich Presence buttons are not visible to yourself in Discord; only other users can see them.
panel.step2: Give it a name (Discord shows that name as the game) and copy the Application ID from General Information.
panel.step3: Keep the bridge running in a terminal:
panel.step4: Upload the images under Rich Presence → Art Assets, then enter their names in the advanced section below.
panel.stepNote: Only the local bridge talks to Discord; the editor itself never connects to it.
preview.iconHint: 512×512 icon: upload it as the application icon in the Discord Developer Portal.
preview.note: Discord takes the app name and icon from your Discord application; the lines below come from this extension.
probe.bridgeOnly: The bridge is running, but Discord is not connected. Start the Discord desktop app.
probe.error: The bridge answered with an error: {message}
probe.offline: The bridge does not answer on 127.0.0.1:52700. Start it with the command below.
status.badAppDetail: Check the Application ID: Discord answered with error 4000 (invalid client id).
status.disabledDetail: Turn it on to show your activity in Discord.
status.discordClosedDetail: Open the Discord desktop app. Presence resumes automatically.
status.missingAppDetail: Paste your Application ID below to start.
status.offlineDetail: Start the bridge in a terminal; the setup steps below show how.
status.unknownDetail: The status appears here after the extension starts.
testFail: Discord did not accept the activity: {error}
